item.title: Clancy Trial Verdict May Hinge on a Single Holdout Juror
item.description: The jury has been deadlocked since at least Tuesday on whether to hold Lindsay Clancy legally responsible for the strangling deaths of her three children.
item.dc:creator: Jenna Russell, Maia Spoto, Mark Arsenault and Jacey Fortin
item.media:description: Lindsay Clancy’s lead defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, said one member of the jury was refusing to “listen to the law" and asked the judge remove the juror from the trial.

item.title: North Carolina Set to Mail The Fall’s First Ballots As Trump Tries to Restrict Them
item.description: A federal judge has temporarily blocked a Postal Service rule that could impede millions of mail voters. The Trump administration has asked the Supreme Court to weigh in.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies
item.media:description: Wake County Board of Elections employees prepare absentee ballots to be mailed in Raleigh, N.C., on Thursday.

item.media:description: Ms. Dubray and Mr. Carbullido near the shore where they had rented jet skis in Long Beach, Calif.

item.title: ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Is a Southern Hit. Just Don’t Call Texas Southern.

item.title: Trump Taps Army Engineering Official as Acting Secretary

item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron

item.media:description: Adam R. Telle, the assistant secretary of the Army for civil works, will take over as the acting Army secretary.

item.title: Trump to Break Ground on Arch Before Getting Approval
item.description: Doug Burgum, the interior secretary, announced plans to start work on the site of the 250-foot-tall triumphal arch. Final approval of the project is still pending.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater and Emily Badger
item.category: White House East Wing and Ballroom (Washington, DC)
item.media:description: President Trump has said that the 250-foot triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery must be taller than the Arc de Triomphe in Paris.

item.title: Holdout Juror Throws the Clancy Murder Case Into Disarray
item.description: The five-week case looked set to end, until the jury sent a note saying that a member refused to recognize the proper definition of reasonable doubt. The defense lawyer said an inquiry was planned for Friday morning.

item.media:description: Judge William Sullivan during deliberations of the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy on Thursday in Plymouth County Superior Court in Plymouth, Mass.

item.title: Proposal for White House Visitor Screening Center Advances

item.title: Missouri Supreme Court Delivers Win for Democrats in Redistricting Case

item.title: JD Vance Says He Wouldn’t Call Iran Conflict a War

item.title: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Allow Mail Voting Limits
